title: Harvest Home
carry_block_text: Take your sheaves to the wagon first.

puzzles.title: Read a factor's share
puzzles.question: Use the season 3 plots in harvest_plots (the starter filters them). Fill in the blanks to model grain by variety, then run anovaTest(). What share of the variation in grain does variety explain?
puzzles.starter_code:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = ____ ~ ____
) %>%
  anovaTest()
puzzles.solution:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ variety
) %>%
  anovaTest()
puzzles.right_feedback: Right: that is variety's share of the spread in grain; the noise row holds the rest.
puzzles.wrong_feedback: Not that one. Check the formula reads grain ~ variety, then read the share column in the variety row.

puzzles.title: Which factor explains most?
puzzles.question: Use the season 3 plots in harvest_plots. Build three one-factor models of grain: by variety, by manure and by block, and run anovaTest() on each. Which factor explains the largest share of the variation in grain?
puzzles.starter_code:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ ____
) %>%
  anovaTest()
puzzles.solution:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ variety
) %>%
  anovaTest()

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ manure
) %>%
  anovaTest()

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ block
) %>%
  anovaTest()
puzzles.right_feedback: Right: its share is the biggest of the three.
puzzles.wrong_feedback: Not that one. Run all three models of grain and compare the share in each factor's own row.

puzzles.title: Which row is largest?
puzzles.question: Use the season 3 plots in harvest_plots. Build one model of grain ~ variety * manure and run anovaTest(). Of the rows above total, which has the largest share of the variation in grain? (Put manure first and the interaction row prints as manure:variety; it is the same row.)
puzzles.starter_code:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)
puzzles.solution:
season_3 <- harvest_plots %>%
  filter(season == 3)

buildModel(
  data = season_3,
  model_type = "linear_regression",
  formula = grain ~ variety * manure
) %>%
  anovaTest()
puzzles.right_feedback: Right: that row holds the biggest share of the variation.
puzzles.wrong_feedback: Not that one. Check the formula is grain ~ variety * manure, then compare the share column across every row except total.
